declared.title: Do cash transfers alleviate common mental disorders in low- and middle-income countries? A systematic review and meta-analysis
declared.foundIn: counter-evidence report reports/money-happiness/counter-evidence.md; OpenAlex search « do cash transfers alleviate common mental disorders low- and middle-income countries » (2026-11-22)

population: 17 randomised trials, 26,794 adults or adolescents living in poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America and South Asia

findings.text: During the programmes, cash transfers lowered depression and anxiety a little

support.sentence: Meta-analysis showed that cash transfers significantly reduced depression and anxiety of recipients (dpooled = -0.10; 95%-CI: -0.15, -0.05; p<0.01).

findings.text: Two to nine years after the programmes ended, the improvement may not last

support.sentence: However, improvements may not be sustained 2-9 years after program cessation (dpooled = -0.05; 95%-CI: -0.14, 0.04; ns).

limits: people living in poverty: basic needs not met, the opposite of the book's population
depression and anxiety, not life satisfaction nor happiness
a temporary transfer that ends, not a lasting rise in income or wealth
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa (regions listed in the abstract)
